note: Merged from eight batch files; two batches interrupted by a usage limit were finished by further independent agents with the same instructions (part names record which).

scores.notes: God appears only as smoke and light over the sanctuary (center-right). The two seraphim (upper center) are hooded human angels with just two wings each, not six, and no wings cover their faces or feet. The right seraph holds tongs with a burning coal, which belongs to v6, so the verse's defining six-wing image is missing.

Bearded Ezekiel in undyed tunic and cloak stands center-left among a valley of skulls and bones, right hand outstretched, dust blowing at right; no God figure in the plain grey sky. Unrequested prop: he holds a blank wooden writing tablet and stylus in his left hand (center), no visible marks on it; painting reaches all four edges and corners are clean.

Icon-style Moses and Aaron with plain gold halos before the camp, pig rooting mid-right, and God shown only as a faceless pillar of cloud over the tabernacle. Aaron's white headband (upper center-left) has a small dark curled scribble at its center that reads as a glyph-like inscription; edges are fully painted.

Ink-and-watercolor: seated mother and child reaching toward rays breaking through cloud (center), terraced village, boats on lake (left), red-cloaked soldier and wood-carriers on road (right), grain basket (lower right); bottom-left and bottom-right corners soft-fade to white paper (style margin, not a flaw). Mother and child are larger than the requested small lower-third placement; a faint grey granulation smudge at the bottom edge near x~85% is not legible lettering.

Boaz with plain, unmarked halo at left and lit doorway with lamps at right as requested; but a kneeling headscarfed woman lighting the lamps (center-right, by the doorway) is not in the present list and in Naomi's house reads as Ruth or Naomi, though the scene's 'lamps being lit' implies a lamp-lighter. No text in the halo, the shawl's zigzag band or the corners; painting reaches all four edges.

Icon-style Jericho: wall collapsing into rubble at center with a crowd climbing through the breach into the city, Joshua (center) and six linen-robed priests (right) blowing raised horns, tents at left. Halos are plain gold with no marks, gold ground runs to all four edges, no lettering in any corner.

Icon-style courtyard with palm (left edge), whitewashed archway with hanging lamp (right), clay jars, a woman holding a child's hand at center and a Roman soldier at the right edge; painting reaches all four borders and the small paper in the red-robed man's hand (right) is blank. Villagers stand in a frontal frieze facing the viewer rather than turned toward the doorway in a half-circle, and the woman with child dominates the center.

Jesus at right with arm raised and mouth open calling; Lazarus in linen wrappings steps out of the dark rock tomb at center-left beside the rolled-back round stone, Martha kneeling in awe at left, crowd around. Painting reaches all four edges; corners clean of marks.

A seated mother and a child raising a hand toward light breaking through the clouds (lower center), with a grain basket, wood bundles, boats on the lake (left), villagers carrying wood and a red-cloaked Roman soldier on the road (right). The settlement is a walled town with a classical domed building rather than a village, and the pair are mid-sized rather than small. No lettering at any edge or corner.

Ezekiel in plain tunic and brown cloak stands center-left in side view with right hand extended over a bone-strewn valley, dust lifting at right; overcast sky (not quite pale and even) holds no figure or face. All four edges painted to the border; no lettering in corners.

Ink-and-watercolor Jonah waist-deep beside the great fish's open, faintly glowing mouth (center), crew at the ship rail top right; the glow has no face or figure and all edges are painted. Minor oddities: a second whale-like hump in the water behind Jonah at left and a sailor in purple with his head hidden at the ship rail.

Icon-style Job with staff and a plain unmarked gold halo stands before a grey ash heap with a dust whirlwind and light breaking through dark cloud above (top center); the whirlwind and radiance contain no face or figure, painting reaches all four edges with no border band. Job is large and faces the viewer rather than small with head raised to the storm, and the walled towns flanking him look intact rather than ruined; two small dot marks on the green jar (lower right) read as pottery decoration, not lettering.

Families carrying children walk the dry path between teal water walls, and Moses with staff stands at the front-left edge; the pillar of fire is only a flame column on the horizon (center), with fire glow in the right water wall and no form. Gold icon ground replaces the night sky, the left wall is lower than the right with sea lapping at Moses' feet; no lettering and all edges painted.

Ink-and-watercolor dark sea with pale light pouring down from the top center (the white paper there is the light source, not a border band) and mist wisps over the water. Zoomed light area and mist show no face, figure or silhouette; dark wash reaches the sides and bottom, no signature in the corners.

A raised gold icon-board border runs around all four sides of the picture, a painted frame. Inside it David reclines on grass with staff, plain halo, harp and sword beside a still pool, with sheep and a hill village, matching the scene; no lettering in the halo or corners.

Empty white-gold throne at center under a rainbow with lightning and cloud, no figure on or around it; lion, ox, six-winged man-faced creature and eagle stand on a glassy crystal floor, lion and eagle covered in eyes (the ox shows few). Minor extras (golden chest before the throne, sashes on the creatures) but no lettering found on chest, robes or wall panels; edges full.

Fire and burning debris stream from the sky onto a mud-brick city (left-center) on a river plain, with dawn sun on the right horizon. No face or figure appears in the fire cloud (top center). Only one distinct city cluster is visible; the right foreground has burning ground but no buildings. No people or lettering.

Icon-style child at center among wolf with lamb, leopard with goat, calf and young lion, staff in foreground, walled town upper left; gold ground reaches all edges and the halo is unmarked. Uncertain because the anonymous child wears a gold nimbus and blue/maroon garments that read as the Christ Child, and a domed Byzantine church building stands at right.

Oil-style elderly man lying dead with eyes closed on a hillside (center-right), two kneeling and two standing mourners, stone well, tents, tools, jar and grazing sheep as requested. He lies on his back rather than his side; all edges and corners are painted with no marks.

Unpeopled landscape: a still, glassy pale lake ringed by ochre/red hills under a burnished gold sky with low cloud at the horizon; reaches all four edges, no lettering, no figure in sky or clouds. Faint white vertical/horizontal glint lines cross the water (center) and tiny dark cypress-like spires sit on the bottom hill, neither reads as text or a figure; no city shown, which the scene text does not require.

Job, dust-stained with a staff, stands on a grey ash heap looking up at a dust whirlwind with bright light behind it (upper center); no face or figure in the cloud or radiance. A walled settlement sits at right, broken pottery lies in the foreground, and the painting reaches all edges with no lettering in the corners.

Walls are fallen and priests (right) blow shofars beside the ark, with Joshua at center, but the whole crowd, children included, streams out of the breach toward the viewer, away from the city, reversing 'went up into the city'. Painted to all edges, no lettering on the ark or in the corners.

Central throne is empty, shown only with radiance, a green rainbow arc, lightning and cloud; the four living creatures (lion, ox, man, eagle) with eye-covered wings flank it on a reflective glassy floor with small thrones at both side edges. The wall friezes are floral ornament with no glyphs; painting reaches all borders, though an unrequested golden chest sits before the throne.

Ink-and-watercolor: Job, bearded with staff, stands on a grey ash heap with broken pottery, face lifted to a spiraling dust whirlwind whose center is only a glow of light (no face or figure). Mud-brick village at right; wash reaches all four borders, pale left sky is painted glow, no signature in corners.

The Shulammite stands left of center holding wildflowers and a basket under a blossoming apple tree, with wild roses (lower left), lilies (lower right), and a vineyard and village in the valley behind. The shepherd's staff stands upright on its own in the open meadow (center) instead of leaning against a tree, which is minor. No lettering in any corner.

Ink-and-watercolor: Abraham stands behind a stacked-stone altar with knife raised in his right hand and face turned up, Isaac (bearded young man) bound with rope on the firewood, single tree at right and valley behind; dawn sky shows only clouds, no figure. The sky wash fades to white paper along the upper-left edge and top-left corner (style-consistent margin); no lettering in corners.

Icon-style twin walled cities burning under streaks of falling fire, with smoke and a bright dawn horizon; God appears only as fire from the sky, with no face in the clouds. A thick painted gold border band frames all four sides, an ornamental frame inside the artwork.

Ink-and-watercolor: Jesus stands at the left end of the boat with arm outstretched over rough foreground waves while the far water is calm; about nine disciples grip the rail and rigging and look toward him, torn sail slackening; left edge and bottom corners soft-fade to white paper (style margin). The hanging lamp (center) is a modern glass-globe hurricane lantern, a small anachronism, and the light reads as overcast day more than night breaking to dawn.

About ten exiles sit bowed on the grass by a river with willows, backs to a walled Babylon with ziggurat-like towers (upper center-right); lyres and a lute lie on the ground at lower left and right, still strung rather than unstrung. Dusk sky, dark vignette but painted to all edges, no lettering found.

Icon style: Saul kneels at center with one arm raised against a cone of light from the top center (no figure inside the light), with five companions shielding their eyes and Damascus at upper right. Halos are plain; a few ~10px ground squiggles near the lower-left and lower-right feet read as grass strokes, not lettering. Minor oddities: two companions have halos, Saul kneels rather than stopping mid-stride, and the city has a domed building with a minaret.

Moses (left foreground) stretches his hand toward a single towering wave on the left, but there is no second wall of water and the middle is a wet, water-filled channel beside a beach where the Israelites stand (right), so it reads as a tidal wave rather than a divided sea with dry ground. The bright cloud break at top center holds no figure or face; no lettering, full edges.

Icon-style: Daniel stands centered in a round stone den with four calm lions, a shaft of light from above and no angel figure; Darius leans over a barred opening at upper left. Halos plain with no marks; no border band; a tiny anonymous bearded onlooker peeks over the wall at the top-left corner and Darius is given a halo, both minor.

At top center, above the rainbow, a faint seated human figure with a head and robe is painted in the radiating light, giving God a form; the throne below is empty. The lion, ox, man and eagle creatures have eyes only on their wings, and the lion and eagle wear robes. The halos are plain and the golden chest's carving is geometric with no lettering.

Icon-style Jericho: priests in white blow long trumpets before a collapsing wall, people shout at left and stream through the breach, Joshua with spear and sword at center, Ark carried at right. A raised gold panel frame with a recessed inner border surrounds the whole painting on all four sides.

Classical David reclines on green grass beside a still pool at sunrise, holding a shepherd's crook, with grazing sheep and a hill village behind; a harp and sheathed sword lie at lower right. God, the verse's shepherd, is not given any form, and the edges are fully painted with no marks.

Ink-and-watercolor: Jesus (center) cries out with right arm raised skyward while a fully bandaged Lazarus strides out of the dark tomb doorway behind him (center-left); stone rolled aside, Martha-like woman in awe (center-right) and mourners spread across the foreground; painting reaches all edges, no lettering. Jesus faces away from the tomb toward the crowd rather than facing it with his arm toward the entrance, and Lazarus is drawn as a striding mummy, which reads slightly horror-movie.

The stone is still in David's sling pouch (center-left) while Goliath is already struck and falling, and Goliath (center-right) is an impossible contortion: upside-down face, arched back, twisted legs and a spear with blades at both ends. He is also no taller than David; armies flank both sides on a gold ground, painted to all edges with no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: a child with a staff stands at center with a hand on a wolf lying beside a lamb; a leopard with a young goat lies lower right and a calf with a lion at right, with a terraced Judean hillside and a walled town gate behind. The sky and left side soft-fade into white paper (style margin, not a frame); the lion is a full-maned adult, and no signature is in any corner.

The concubine lying on the mat (lower right) has open, alert eyes gazing upward, so she reads as a living woman about to be stabbed rather than a still body; the 'interior' is also roofless with a gold daylight sky over a broken wall while the door and window show night. Levite with knife, lamp, bench, jars and saddled donkey in the doorway are present; no lettering, full edges.

A painted signature reading roughly 'Tasiak' sits in the bottom-right corner on the dark column base. Faint seated hooded figure with a pale head and arm is visible on zoom inside the curtained sanctuary doorway below the right seraph (center, ~x830 y400); the two seraphim show four wings, cover faces with hands, and leave feet bare.

Goliath (right) is upside-down in a cartwheel, head and hands at the ground and sandaled legs in the air, rather than falling forward on his face; he is barely larger than David. Both armies (left and right hills) are identical red-crested Greek hoplites, so the Israelites cannot be told apart. The watercolor wash fades to white paper at the top-left and top-right corners.

Icon-style exiles (men and women) sit grieving on a riverbank, two lyres hang on a willow at upper left (not on the ground as requested), Babylon walls and ziggurats across the river. A raised gold panel frame borders the painting on all four sides.

Icon-style haloed Moses with staff before parted walls of water, Israelites at both sides, rays breaking through dark clouds with no divine figure. A painted gold frame borders all four edges; Moses stretches his arm toward the crowd at left rather than over the sea, and the scene reads as daylight, not night.

Icon style: Isaiah (bottom center) looks up at two hovering winged seraphim before a carved sanctuary with incense smoke; no divine figure in the smoke or light, gold ground reaches all edges. But the left seraph already holds tongs with a burning coal (the later v.6 moment), both seraphim show bare uncovered feet against the verse, and Isaiah grips two separate staffs, one in each hand.

A raised gold painted frame borders all four sides of the image. Moses (left, plain halo) stretches his hand over a sea split into two cliff-like walls with wind-blown spray, Israelites gather at both sides, and God appears only as a cloud with rays at top center (no form); scene is gold daylight rather than night, with an unexplained walled city at upper right.

The landscape is inset between plain gold vertical bands (~25-30px) running the full height of the left and right edges, which reads as a border band. Ezekiel stands among the bones with one hand out but is writing on a blank tablet with a stylus instead of only speaking. God appears only as faint wind swirls in the gold sky.

Goliath (right center) topples backward rather than onto his face, the stone bounces away above his head instead of sinking in, and a second helmet flies off while he still wears one. Both armies are identical red-crested hoplites with plain shields; David with sling and bag at left, full edges, no lettering.

Saul halted mid-stride at center with both hands raised against a blazing shaft of light from the clouds (no figure in the light), companions crouching and shielding their eyes, dropped staffs, walled Damascus behind. All four edges painted, corners clean.

Jesus on the cross (top center) still wears a white tunic and a full blue mantle while soldiers divide the same blue garment on the ground (bottom center), so the clothing state contradicts itself. His cross-nimbus halo has small glyph-like marks in its arms; the titulus board is blank.

Ink-and-watercolor: four crouching Roman soldiers around spread garments, one raising a stick-lot, Jesus crucified on a cross at upper right, Jerusalem walls and small onlookers at left. The titulus board atop the cross (upper right) carries small grey glyph-like marks; washes fade to white paper along the left and bottom edges and top-left corner (style-consistent).

Classical bald Elisha in a fur mantle on a rocky road below a walled town, with six jeering youths pointing and kicking dust at right and a gold shrine with a calf idol on the hilltop; edges are painted and there is no lettering. He walks down toward the viewer, away from the gate, and looks away from the mockers, so the 'going up' direction is not shown.

Ink-and-watercolor high view over a plain: flaming sulfur meteors with smoke trails streak down onto a walled mud-brick city and set fields alight, palms and dry scrub in the foreground, no people; bottom-left corner fades to white paper (style margin), no lettering. Only one city is shown where the verse and scene name both Sodom and Gomorrah.

Peter leaps from the boat clutching a cloak around himself, mid-air over a splash (center), the beloved disciple points from the boat at right, and Jesus stands on the shore by a small charcoal fire at left. Misty dawn lake; textured pale sky at top-left is painted to the edge, and there is no lettering anywhere.

A raised gold painted frame borders all four edges of the icon. Christ's cross-nimbus (upper right) carries Greek-style letters in its three arms. The scene otherwise matches: Jesus stands at the stern with an arm outstretched, disciples crouch in the boat, and the waves are rough at left and calm at right; the oil lamp hangs on the outside of the hull.

Ink-and-watercolor wide landscape of calm, glassy water between low tan hills under soft clear light, unpeopled; the left edge and top-right corner fade softly to white paper (style margin). Small pen squiggles along the shoreline at bottom right are terrain hatching, not lettering; no figure appears in the clouds.

The mother and child are painted as a Virgin-and-Child icon (haloed Madonna in starred red maphorion, haloed Christ child), introducing Mary and Jesus into a generic Romans 8:28 scene; the child's cross-nimbus carries letter glyphs ('O', 'O', 'Π'-like) in its arms. Child sits facing the viewer rather than lifting a hand to the light; village, boats, wood carriers, grain basket and soldier at right are present; edges full.

Abraham (center) raises a knife in his right hand with his face lifted, his other hand on Isaac, who lies bound on firewood atop a stone altar on a scrubby ridge with a single tree (left) and a valley (right). The halos are plain gold rings, and the gold sky shows only leaf-texture scratches, with no figure or lettering.

Villagers, including a child holding a woman's hand, stand in a stone courtyard facing an open arched doorway at right; a Roman legionary walks in the background left, water jars and palms present. Tympanum over the door is an interlaced lattice grille, not lettering; painting reaches all four edges; group is a cluster rather than a half-circle.

Icon-style temple interior: Isaiah with staff looks up at two flying seraphim, and the divine presence appears only as smoke and glow with no figure. Solid maroon border bands with a cream fillet line run down the full left and right edges; the seraphim show two to four wings with faces and feet uncovered, and the left one carries a coal in tongs (from v.6).

Ink-and-watercolor dawn lakeshore: Peter (center) leaps from the boat clutching his cloak over a splash, the beloved disciple points from the boat (right), Jesus stands on the stony shore by a small fire (left); top corners and bottom-left soft-fade to white paper (style margin), no lettering. Jesus is close and mid-sized rather than small in the distance, but the moment reads clearly.

Abraham stands left of center with the knife raised, face lifted, beside a stone altar where Isaac lies bound with rope on stacked wood (right), on a ridge above a deep valley with a single tree. Divine presence is only sun rays through cloud at top right, with no form; painted to all edges, no lettering.

Night oil painting: Peter steps from the boat's gunwale (left) onto the waves toward a softly haloed Jesus standing on the water at right-center, with disciples and a lit oil lamp in the boat and a shore village at right. Dark paint reaches every edge, no lettering in the corners; Peter oddly carries a coiled net on his shoulder.

Icon-style: bald, haloed Elisha in a fur mantle strides on the rocky road at lower left while seven youths at the walled town gate (right) point and jeer, with a golden calf shrine on the rise at top center; painting reaches all borders. The plain halo carries no marks, and the faint relief on the calf's pedestal reads as carving ornament, not writing.

Night crossing: families carrying children walk a wet, stony seabed between towering curling water walls toward a pillar of flame on the far shore (pure fire, no figure inside); white-bearded Moses with staff stands at left foreground, arm low. Dark paint reaches all four edges; corners clean.

David reclines on the grass beside a still pool, holding a staff, with sheep grazing and resting and hilltop villages behind; a harp and sword are added. A short second stick lies by his foot (lower right), out of line with the staff he holds, which is minor. The halo is plain and there is no lettering.

Daniel stands calm at center of a round stone den with lions lying mouths-closed on both sides, Darius in crown and purple robe leans over the rim at upper right, barred wooden lid at upper left. The shaft of light from above (top center) contains no figure or face; satchel at Daniel's hip is plain; all edges painted.

Square icon of the haloed Shulammite holding wildflowers among roses, lilies, a flowering tree and a leaning shepherd's crook; the halo is plain. The square artwork is pillarboxed: the left and right quarters of the frame are blurred enlarged filler bands, so the painting does not reach the side borders.

The painting is a portrait-format icon panel set in the middle of the frame with wide blank gold bands filling the left and right ~27% on each side, so the artwork does not reach the side edges. Inside the panel the scene matches: the Shulammite in a red mantle with a plain outline halo holds roses and lilies beside a blossoming tree, a shepherd's staff leans against it, and vineyards lie behind her; no lettering in the halo or on the embroidery.

Watercolor village courtyard with arch, palm, water jars, a woman holding a child's hand, and a figure reading a book (blank pages) in the dark doorway at left; but the villagers stand in a line facing the viewer rather than turned toward the doorway, and there are two Roman soldiers (left by the door, far right). The bottom and left edges fade to white paper (style-consistent margin); ink marks on the wall and ground are stone and pebble outlines, not lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: the Shulammite stands left of center holding roses and lilies in a flowered meadow, with a blossoming tree behind, a vineyard and hill village beyond, and a shepherd's crook standing in the grass at right. Painted to all four edges (top right is pale sky, not a band), and no signature in the corners.

Ink-and-watercolor: priests in white and violet blow horn-trumpets at right before collapsed mudbrick ramparts in dust, Joshua with spear and sword at center, crowds streaming through the breach and tents at left; the bottom edge and bottom corners fade to white paper (style margin). No lettering in corners; the foreground group walks toward the viewer rather than into the city.

Ink-and-watercolor interior: a grim grey-bearded man kneels beside a woman's still body on a mat, knife raised in his right hand before any cut, oil lamp on a stool at right, clay jars, saddled donkey in the night doorway behind. Non-graphic; wash reaches all four edges and corners are free of marks.

Exiles sit weeping with heads in their hands on a grassy riverbank at dusk (foreground), with Babylonian walls and ziggurats across the water and lyres on the ground. The lyres are strung and the trees are palms rather than willows; small patches of white paper show at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners (watercolor fade). No lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: Saul at center halts with hand at brow under a blaze of rays (no figure in the light), four companions with staffs shield their eyes, walled Damascus behind (with an anachronistic domed building and two minaret-like towers, upper right). Pen squiggles on the road read as cursive-like glyph marks in the bottom-left corner and bottom-right, likely ground texture but resembling a signature; sky wash shows a little white paper at the top-right edge.

Ink-and-watercolor bald Elisha in a fur mantle at lower left, four youths pointing and jeering mid-right, more townspeople at the gate, and a golden calf on a plinth on the rise. The edges fade softly to white paper (lower left and right corners, left side), which is style-consistent. Elisha walks down toward the viewer away from the gate, not up toward it.

Icon style: a plain gilt border band runs down the left, right and bottom edges (clearly visible at both bottom corners) enclosing the painted scene, so the painting does not reach the borders. Scene itself matches: Peter mid-leap clutching his cloak over ripples (center), beloved disciple pointing from the boat with nets and oar (left), Jesus small on the shore by a charcoal fire (right); no halos or lettering.

The grey-haired father, robe flying and one leg trailing behind, embraces the ragged younger son at the neck in the center of a dusty road between olive trees and stone houses, with hills and lake behind. A columned classical temple at right is an odd detail but not a blocker; painted to all edges, no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor: a grey-bearded father with a flying cloak, one leg kicked back mid-run, embraces a weary young son on a stone road, with terraced hills, a walled farmstead, a columned building and lake boats behind. The sky and bottom-left corner soft-fade to cream paper (style margin, no frame), with no signature. Both figures' feet stride left together, which slightly blurs who ran to whom.

Icon-style: the old man lies on his back on a rock slab at center, with eleven mourners kneeling and standing around him, a stone well and jar at left, crossed tools at bottom left, sheep and a village at the back; no halos or lettering, and the painting reaches all borders. The composition echoes a Dormition icon (the central blue-robed kneeler has a stock Christ-type face, and there is a woman in a red maphorion), but nothing marks them as named figures; the scene's tents are missing.

A raised gold icon border frames the painting on all four sides (gold band with an inset bevel at top, bottom, left and right). Inside, bearded exiles sit grieving on a grassy riverbank with lyres on the ground, willows and palms, Babylon's walls and ziggurats across the river; no lettering found.

The throne (center) is empty, and the doorway behind shows only rainbow light and lightning, with no divine figure; the four eye-covered creatures stand on a glassy sea. White-bearded elders, an unselected recurring cast entry, sit on the thrones at the far left and right edges, and the man creature (center-right) reads as a full robed man standing in front of a separate spotted, winged quadruped body. The lion also wears a robe.

Unpeopled luminous landscape with a still, glassy lake winding through flowering land and rocks, radiant pale sky above; the bright sky center holds only light and wisps of cloud, no face or figure. Painted to all four edges, no lettering.

Classical Roman soldiers crouch around garments on rocky ground, one raising a hand, with helmets beside them, Jesus crucified on a hill at upper left and distant onlookers and city walls at right; all edges are painted. The tiny pale title board atop the cross (upper left) carries faint grey marks that may read as illegible lettering, but they are too faint to call with confidence.

Ink-and-watercolor: bearded Ezekiel in tunic and rough cloak stands center-left with outstretched hand over a valley strewn with skulls and bones; corners and top soft-fade to white paper (style margin). In the ground just below his feet at the bottom edge (about x 32%, y 97%) a small cursive scribble reads like handwritten letters 'ovis' with a dotted i, and he also holds an unrequested blank writing tablet and stylus.

Daniel stands calm at center among five resting, closed-mouthed lions, and Darius in a purple robe with a gold ring leans over the den rim at upper left. The angel and God appear only as a soft arched glow behind Daniel's head with no figure; the heavy lid and gate are missing and the sky reads as daylight. Watercolor painted to all edges, no lettering.

Dark oil interior: the grim Levite kneels with a knife raised beside the still, unmarked body of the concubine lying on a mat, lit by a small lamp, with a moonlit window and a saddled donkey in the doorway at right; no gore. Painted to all edges with no lettering; the donkey's saddle has a horn and stirrups (anachronistic).

Ink-and-watercolor night storm: Peter, with a net over his shoulder, steps off the boat's side with a bare foot on the waves (left center), looking toward a softly lit Jesus standing on the water at right, with disciples and an oil lamp in the boat; washes reach all four edges. No lettering; Peter oddly carries a staff, and Jesus stands fairly near rather than small and distant.

Gold painted icon frame surrounds the image on all four sides, and Jesus' cross-nimbus (top center) carries the letters 'Ο', 'Θ', 'Ν'. Jesus stands mid-boat with arm outstretched over disciples, torn sail, rough waves left and calm ripples right; the oil lamp hangs on the outside of the hull.

The whole image is enclosed by a painted gold border, there is a monogram signature in the water at the bottom-right corner, and Jesus's cross-nimbus (right) has glyph-like marks. Twelve men sit in the boat besides Peter, who is stepping out (center), so there are 13 disciples, and the long-haired one at the right of the boat looks like a second Jesus.

Moses with staff and Aaron stand side by side in the foreground facing the viewer, a pig roots in straw at right, tents, tabernacle and Israelites at a distance; a smoke column over the tabernacle has no figure in it. Aaron wears an ornate ephod and gemmed breastpiece (not the plain linen requested), stones show no legible marks; edges painted to the border.

Classical Boaz with a staff stands at left in a mud-brick courtyard at dusk, with a stone bench, water jars and an open doorway at right; edges are fully painted and the shawl bands are plain weave. An anonymous headscarfed woman crouches at the doorway lighting a clay lamp; she does the requested lamp-lighting but could be read as Ruth.

Painterly night storm: a huge toothed fish rises open-mouthed (center) beside Jonah, who is waist-deep in the waves (center-right), while nine sailors grip the ship's rail (upper left) under lightning; the glow at upper right is only mist and spray with no face or figure, and the painting reaches all edges with no lettering. Jonah is turned away from the mouth with a hand on its jaw, reading more like escaping than being taken in.

Jesus' cruciform halo (upper center-right) carries the Greek letters 'O θ N' in the cross arms, which is visible lettering. Otherwise the scene fits: Jesus raises his arm toward the tomb at center-left, Lazarus walks out in white grave linens with a plain halo, the great stone is rolled back, and the crowd with Martha stands on both sides; gold ground, painted to all edges.

Icon style: the elderly father in a brown robe embraces his gaunt, barefoot son around the neck on a dirt road at center, with a walled village and gate at left and the lake with boats and nets at right. Both have plain thin-line halos with no marks, the gold sky and landscape reach all four edges, and there is no lettering in the corners.

Ink-and-watercolor: an old white-bearded man lies dead on the grass at center, with six relatives in plain tunics kneeling or standing with bowed heads, and a stone well, clay jar and tools at right, tents and mud-brick houses behind, and sheep at left under golden late light. The washes reach all four edges, and there is no lettering in the corners.

Viewed from the bow, Jesus stands on the stern deck with right arm outstretched under breaking storm clouds; about twelve disciples sit around the hull looking at him, torn sail on the mast, a lamp burning on the deck, sea still choppy. Painted to all four edges; corners clean.

Concentric rays and arcs of light rise from the horizon (top center) against a gold-leaf sky over dark, empty, rolling waters with wisps of mist; there is no face, hand or figure in the radiance. The light sits on the horizon rather than coming from above the frame, which is minor. No lettering in any corner.

Ink-and-watercolor night crossing: a long column of families carrying children walks the dry seabed between towering water walls, Moses with staff and lowered arm at right foreground. The orange fire glow at top center is flame and smoke only, with no face or figure; dark washes reach all four edges, no lettering.

Ink-and-watercolor Boaz with a shepherd's crook stands at left in an evening courtyard between mud-brick houses, with a stone bench, jar and lit lamp on a table at right; the painting reaches all four borders and the shawl bands are geometric weave only. As in the requested lamp-lighting, an anonymous headscarfed woman crouches lighting a lamp at the doorway.

Icon style: Jesus (right) wears a cross-nimbus with Greek-like letters (O, Ω/6 shape, N/K) painted in its arms, and haloed disciples crowd the boat (left) while Peter steps over the gunwale toward him; painting reaches all edges. The sky is flat gold daylight rather than the requested night, though the moment itself reads clearly.

Dark rolling waters fill the lower frame and a pale burst of light breaks on the horizon left of center, with mist curling at right; brightened, the light and mist show no face, figure or hand. Only a slight darkening at the borders, painted to all four edges, no lettering.

Gold painted border strips with a dark ruled inner line run down the full left and right edges (and frame the bottom corners), forming a frame around the icon. Inside, Israelite families walk the dry seabed between towering blue water walls and Moses stands with a staff at right; God's presence appears only as orange flames within each water wall, with no face or figure, and Moses' halo is plain. The gold sky shows no night.

Ink-and-watercolor: David reclines on a flowered pasture holding a staff, with a harp and sword at lower left, sheep around him, a still pool and a hill village behind, and a low sun at upper right. The only margin is a faint sliver where the sky wash fades to white paper at the top-right corner (style margin); there is no lettering in the corners.

Ink-and-watercolor: white-bearded Moses at left foreground raises his staff toward the sea while Israelite families crowd the beach at right, under storm clouds with a glow of light (no figure in it). The sea is not divided: waves simply break onto an ordinary shoreline, with no walls of water or dry path, so the verse's central event is missing.

A small child stands centered among a wolf resting with a lamb (left), a leopard with a young goat (center), a calf and a young lion (right), with a shepherd's staff on the ground in the foreground. Behind are a terraced stone village with a town gate on the ridge and dawn sky. No lettering in any corner.

Icon-style Jonah with an unmarked halo stands waist-deep beside the great fish's open, glowing mouth, sailors hauling on the ship at left, dark storm clouds and lightning at upper right over a gold ground (night not conveyed). The glow inside the fish's mouth holds no figure; dark seaweed scrollwork fills the underwater bottom area but is part of the scene, not a separate border; edges painted to the border.

Ink-and-watercolor Moses with a crook and Aaron in a blue ephod stand side by side in the foreground, a pig roots in the sand at center, Israelites stand at right, and the tabernacle and tents recede behind them. God appears only as a faceless column of smoke over the tabernacle. Aaron's headband and breastplate stones carry no marks, and the lower-left corner and left edge fade softly to white paper, which suits the style.

Icon panel with a raised gilt frame border on all four sides; Jesus' cross-nimbus has lettering (O, O, IG-like glyphs) in its arms, and a faint scribble sits in the ground at bottom right. Bandaged Lazarus stands in front of the round stone, which still sits inside the tomb opening rather than rolled away, and Jesus faces the viewer with his hand raised skyward instead of toward the tomb, with Martha and a crowd at the right.

The two seraphim (upper left and right) have about four wings each, not six, and their bare feet hang uncovered, so the verse's defining detail is wrong; the left seraph already holds tongs with a burning coal from verse 6. Isaiah stands in the foreground before an incense altar and gilded sanctuary door, the divine presence is only light and smoke from above with no form, and the image is painted to all edges with no lettering.

A raised gold frame borders all four edges, and Christ's cross-nimbus (upper right) has an 'O' glyph in each of its three arms. Otherwise it matches: Peter, clothed in his wrapped cloak, leaps from the boat into the surf at center, the beloved disciple points from the boat at left with a plain halo, and Jesus stands by a charcoal fire on the shore.

A raised gold icon-board border frames all four sides of the picture, a painted frame. Inside it, fire and lightning-like streaks rain from a gold sky onto two walled cities (center and right) on a farmed plain, with the sun at dawn over the eastern hills and no people. The sky holds only flame and smoke with no face or figure, and there is no lettering.
